question: A 17-year-old presents with moderate acne — multiple inflammatory papules and pustules with a few comedones, no nodules or cysts. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial pharmacological approach?

answers.text: Topical benzoyl peroxide + topical retinoid (e.g., adapalene) — addressing both P. acnes and comedonal components

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Moderate inflammatory acne without nodules/cysts is treated with topical combination therapy: benzoyl peroxide (bactericidal, no resistance risk) plus a retinoid (normalises keratinisation, prevents comedone formation). Adding topical clindamycin is acceptable but should always be combined with benzoyl peroxide to minimise resistance.

answers.text: Oral isotretinoin 0.5 mg/kg/day for 16–20 weeks — targeting all four pathogenic mechanisms

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Oral isotretinoin is reserved for severe nodulo-cystic acne, acne unresponsive to 6 months of conventional therapy, or acne causing significant scarring. It is not first-line for moderate inflammatory acne.

answers.text: Topical corticosteroid cream — reducing inflammation at the lesion site

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Topical corticosteroids are NOT used for acne vulgaris. They promote follicular occlusion and can cause steroid acne — they worsen rather than treat acne.

answers.text: Oral tetracycline monotherapy — targeting P. acnes directly

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Oral antibiotics alone are not recommended for acne; they should always be combined with benzoyl peroxide or a retinoid to reduce the risk of antibiotic resistance. Monotherapy also does not address the comedonal component.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Acne Vulgaris block. The four acne pathogenic factors are: sebum overproduction, P. acnes colonisation, follicular hyperkeratosis, and inflammation. Combination topical therapy addresses both comedonal and inflammatory components — oral isotretinoin is reserved for severe or refractory disease.

Well done. The acne step-up algorithm: mild (topical only) → moderate (topical combination ± oral antibiotic) → severe nodulo-cystic (oral isotretinoin). Benzoyl peroxide + retinoid is the cornerstone of moderate acne management.
